claims.statement: The definitive CBAM regime has applied since 1 January 2026 and requires covered importers above the stated mass threshold to become authorised declarants, declare embedded emissions, and surrender certificates.

Certificate prices are officially published and tied to EU ETS auction prices, so procurement and finance teams face a recurring, quantifiable exposure that can be estimated from validated import data.

Hypothesis: indirect customs representatives and freight forwarders are a lower-friction reseller channel than selling separately to each importer because the compliance packet can be attached to an import workflow they already administer.

contrary_evidence: A 50-tonne threshold removes many smaller importers from the core obligation and narrows the initial addressable base.
The Commission supplies extensive sector guidance and registry tooling, so the defensible value is cross-company evidence collection and validation, not regulatory information.

economics.acquisition_route: Sign specialist customs advisers for one covered sector, then let each partner activate its importer portfolio
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 35 brokers averaging 100000 PLN ARR plus packet fees could reach 5 million PLN ARR across the EU in years 5-7; at 25% EBITDA, 6x EBITDA, and 75% ownership, founder equity would be about 5.6 million PLN, with upside from supplier-network density
economics.founder_time: 18-25 hours weekly during sector-template and first-broker integration work, then target 10-12 hours weekly with partner-led onboarding
economics.gross_margin_basis: Document ingestion and workflow software can reach 75-88% gross margin; multilingual exception support and expert review are the main variable costs
economics.payback: Target under 9 months per broker; importer value comes from avoiding manual supplier chasing and quantifying certificate exposure earlier
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 150-500 PLN per supplier-shipment packet plus 30000-120000 PLN annual broker platform licence
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual declarations, repeated imports, changing certificate prices, and persistent supplier profiles create recurring use

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable supplier-installation profiles, provenance chains, sector error patterns, and broker integrations reduce repeated evidence cost
fingerprint.customer: EU customs brokers, freight forwarders, authorised CBAM declarants, and importers of covered goods
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embedded or white-labelled in customs broker and freight-forwarder job-management portals
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Multi-party supplier evidence exchange, validation engine, and registry-packet workspace sold through brokers
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Broker or importer pays per covered supplier-shipment packet and annual entity workspace
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A covered import job lacks verified supplier emissions and cost-exposure evidence needed for annual CBAM compliance

founder_fit: Strong quantitative, EU, automation, and evidence-provenance fit. The broker-channel design reduces founder-led sales, while multilingual supplier requests can be automated. Sector methodology and legal sign-off should be contracted rather than improvised.
risks: Incorrect emissions data can create certificate and enforcement exposure; a verifier or declarant must remain accountable.
Large customs platforms may bundle the function rapidly.
Cross-border supplier onboarding could become a high-touch service burden.

structure.control_point: The broker-managed compliance packet joining a customs job to supplier emissions provenance
structure.critical_dependency: Accurate supplier data acquisition and broker acceptance of a clear human-verification and liability boundary

thesis: Create a CBAM supplier-evidence exchange that customs brokers and freight forwarders can embed in import jobs. It would request production data from non-EU suppliers, validate it against sector templates, preserve provenance, calculate certificate exposure scenarios, and hand a human declarant a registry-ready packet.
title: Carbon Packet Relay
uncertainties: The fraction of brokers willing to assume a reseller role and their liability boundaries are unknown.
Supplier response rates and primary emissions-data quality may be too low for automation.
Registry interfaces and verifier expectations may change as the definitive regime matures.
